title: Gammon in Cider
subtitle: Gammon joint simmered in cider then glazed with honey and mustard
excerpt: A whole gammon joint gently poached in cider and aromatics until tender, then finished in a hot oven with a sticky honey and mustard glaze. Equally good hot or cold.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gammon is a cured leg of pork, similar to ham but sold raw and cooked by the buyer rather than the producer. It has been a staple of British cooking for centuries, historically salted and dried to preserve it through the winter. The tradition of cooking gammon in cider is strongest in the West Country (Somerset, Herefordshire, Devon), where cider production has been central to rural life for over a thousand years. The acidity of the cider gently tenderises the meat and rounds out the saltiness of the cure. The honey and mustard glaze applied at the end is a Victorian refinement that became the standard finish. Cold glazed gammon is one of the most reliable cold meats for Christmas and celebration tables.

recipeTools.notes: A large pot deep enough to submerge the gammon.

content.text: If the gammon is heavily salted, soak it in cold water for several hours or overnight before cooking, changing the water once. This reduces the saltiness. The simmering liquid should be kept at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil, which can tighten the meat. Score the fat in a diamond pattern before glazing so the glaze can penetrate and the fat renders and crisps.

items.preparation: bone-in joint, soaked if very salty

content.text: Place the gammon in a large pot. Add the cider, onion, carrot, bay, peppercorns, and cloves. Add enough cold water to just cover. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Simmer gently for 20 minutes per 500 g (so about 80 minutes for a 2 kg joint). Top up with water if needed.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Mix the honey, mustard, and brown sugar in a small bowl. Lift the gammon from the pot onto a roasting tin. Peel off and discard the skin. Score the fat in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife.

Spoon or brush the glaze over the fat. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until the fat is caramelised and golden, basting once halfway through. Rest for 15 minutes before carving. Serve hot or cool completely and serve cold.
